chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: The 91-year-old family friend who remembered his joining Henderson
summary: The woman with the player piano, now 91 and still a jazz fan, remembered when he joined Fletcher Henderson.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yes, but let me tell you about this.
You finish it up the player piano.

Yes. Well, the player piano -- this lady here, B. Walker comes by the house. There's a lady out here wants to see Joe. So I said, 'Well, fine.' Some pretty little chick stop by to see me, you know, even my wife can't resist that. You know I'm home but second time in 22 years. And had a most delicate and complete surprise I ever had in my life. This lady in our home we played -- she had two daughters -- Piano Rose (or piano rolls). Our families, they all knew each other. This lady was 91 years old. Her name was Mrs. Gleason Neesen, now her name is Mrs. Lipscomb (?) and she's still a jazz fan. And to bring me up to date, she said I know when you joined Fletcher Henderson. It was tremendous.
